stories.headline: Hugging Face Explores a Sale at $13 Billion or More — Nearly Triple Its 2023 Valuation
stories.key_takeaway: Hugging Face has hired a bank to gauge buyer interest at $13 billion or more — nearly triple its 2023 valuation — but no bidder has been named and no deal reached.

pull_quote.text: We're building a platform for the community, and they're trusting us with sharing their data and their models on the platform, so we have a long-term responsibility to them.

stories.article_excerpt: Hugging Face — the model hub most of the AI industry treats as public infrastructure, and that almost nobody owns a piece of — is testing what it is worth.

stories.headline: Nvidia Is in Talks to Back Perplexity at More Than $30 Billion — a 50% Markup in a Year
stories.key_takeaway: Nvidia is reportedly negotiating an equity stake in Perplexity at over $30 billion — a 50%-plus markup in twelve months — on the strength of a $750 million revenue figure at least one outlet disputes.

pull_quote.text: No. OpenAI will pay the lease.

stories.article_excerpt: Nvidia is in discussions to invest in Perplexity as part of an equity round that would value the AI search company at more than $30 billion.

stories.headline: XPeng's Robot Unit Raised $900 Million at $6.3 Billion — But Only $600 Million Came From Outside Investors
stories.key_takeaway: XPeng carved its robotics arm into a subsidiary called Dogotix at a $6.3 billion post-money valuation, but a third of the headline $900 million comes from XPeng itself and its own executives.

pull_quote.text: Over the past 12 years, XPENG has remained committed to full-stack in-house R&D, building a solid technological foundation for the physical AI era—across our physical world foundation model, Turing AI chips, and AI infrastructure.

stories.article_excerpt: About an hour before it reported second-quarter results on Monday, XPeng dropped the bigger news: its robotics business is now a separate company.

stories.headline: Amazon Raised Echo, Kindle and Fire TV Prices by Up to 60% — Squeezed by the Same AI Buildout It's Funding
stories.key_takeaway: Amazon abandoned its long-running loss-leader hardware strategy overnight, raising Echo, Kindle, Fire TV and eero prices by up to 60% because AI data centers have absorbed the memory supply its cheap devices depended on.

pull_quote.text: The consumer electronics industry is facing significant increases in memory and storage component costs. After absorbing these increases for as long as we could, we recently adjusted pricing across our product lines.

data_points.label: High-end memory output to data centers

stories.article_excerpt: The cheapest Amazon Echo is no longer cheap. Over the weekend of August 21, without an announcement, prices moved across four product lines.

stories.headline: Quintessent Raises $40M Betting One Laser Can Replace Eight Inside AI Data Centers
stories.key_takeaway: Quintessent's $40M Series A funds a quantum-dot comb laser that emits eight DWDM wavelengths from a single chip, attacking both the indium phosphide shortage and the component-count fragility of optical links in AI clusters.

pull_quote.text: Quintessent is starting its transition from tech development to a product-focused company.

stories.article_excerpt: Every optical link inside a large AI cluster is a small, fragile machine: a laser, a modulator, control electronics and a fiber, all of which can fail.

stories.headline: A Stealth Model Topped a Coding Benchmark on 10 Tasks. Then Someone Ran the Full Set.
stories.key_takeaway: Ox Alpha's viral 80% DeepSWE score came from a 10-task sample; the full run put it roughly level with GPT-5.6 Sol — after thousands of developers had already sent proprietary code to a lab nobody could name.

pull_quote.text: I ran this thing through 10 tasks on DeepSWE (so there could be a ton of variance in it's real score, this is a subset), but uh... gpt-5.6-sol: 52% / fable: 65% / whatever the hell this is: 80%. I am very confused

data_points.label: Tasks in the full DeepSWE set

stories.article_excerpt: On August 21, developer Ben Davis posted a screenshot that ricocheted around AI Twitter within the hour. An anonymous model was beating everything.

stories.headline: Alibaba Shipped Wan3.0 One Day After a $10.2 Billion Share Sale. Net Income Fell 76%.
stories.key_takeaway: Alibaba raised $10.2 billion in equity and shipped its longest video model in the same week its net income fell 76% on a 75% capex surge — trading current profit for position in generative video.

pull_quote.text: In order to be able to capture that future growth, we first need to make these capex investments to build out the necessary compute capacity.

stories.article_excerpt: Alibaba Cloud made Wan3.0 generally available on Monday, August 24. The day before, the company priced 710 million new shares.

stories.headline: ChatGPT Ads Went Live in 31 European Markets. Free and Go Users Are the Product.
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI turned on advertising for ChatGPT Free and Go users across 31 European markets, running contextual ads under GDPR 'legitimate interest' and personalized ads on opt-in consent — a consent-or-pay structure Irish regulators have not yet blessed.

pull_quote.text: It almost feels like people are having to pay if they don't want to receive ads at all.
pull_quote.role: Head of Data Privacy, Arbor Law

stories.article_excerpt: As of this morning, a person in Munich or Milan asking ChatGPT which laptop to buy may get a sponsored answer alongside the real one.

stories.headline: Google's A2A Joins Anthropic's MCP Under One Roof. The Agent Protocol War Ended Before It Started.
stories.key_takeaway: Google's A2A now sits alongside Anthropic's MCP inside the Linux Foundation-directed Agentic AI Foundation — either genuine neutral standardization, or the eight companies with the most to gain quietly agreeing on the agent interoperability layer.

pull_quote.text: Interoperability only expands that already existing trust gap. While the protocol standardizes the pipe, organizations decide what travels through it.

stories.article_excerpt: The protocol war every conference panel spent 2025 predicting is over, and the anticlimax is the story.

stories.headline: AWS Put a Price on Grounding: $7 per 1,000 Agent Web Searches
stories.key_takeaway: AWS's expansion of AgentCore Web Search to Ireland and Tokyo, plus per-call domain and date filters, turns retrieval into a metered utility at $7 per 1,000 queries — undercutting rival grounding APIs and squeezing independent search vendors.

pull_quote.text: What we value most is that AWS uses its own search index and keep queries within our trusted AWS environment.
pull_quote.role: Senior Director of AI & Innovation, Gen Digital

stories.article_excerpt: Grounding an AI agent in the live web now has a sticker price: $7 per 1,000 queries.

stories.headline: Agent Memory Became a Benchmark Category in 2026 — Then the Benchmarks Started Failing Their Own Audits
stories.key_takeaway: Agent memory now has a real leaderboard with forty-point gaps between systems, but independent audits show the dominant benchmark has a scoring bug rendering roughly a quarter of it unscorable — so the gaps may measure the test more than the systems.

pull_quote.text: A system that refuses correctly is penalized identically to a system that hallucinates an answer.

data_points.label: Share of LoCoMo unscorable by construction
LoCoMo accuracy from plain filesystem ops
Works coded in the Always-On Agents survey

stories.article_excerpt: In 2023, "agent memory" meant pasting the chat log back into the prompt. In 2026 it is a leaderboard, with gaps wide enough to sell against.

stories.headline: Multi-Agent Systems Are Wired Wrong. Two Papers Rewire Them at Runtime — A Third Asks If It Matters.
stories.key_takeaway: DyTopo and SYMPHONY show that rewiring agent communication at runtime beats fixed topologies by wide margins, but neither runs the one control — a single strong model at equal token budget — that a Stanford study says makes most multi-agent gains disappear.

pull_quote.text: This suggests that communication topology should be an adaptive object, conditioned on the round-level goal, rather than a static design choice.
pull_quote.role: Lu et al., Peking University / Georgia Tech / Tsinghua

data_points.label: Llama-3-8B on Math-500, single vs dynamic
Single vs multi-agent at matched budget
AgentPrune vs SOTA cost, comparable MMLU

stories.article_excerpt: Hand Llama-3-8B-Instruct a set of hard math problems and it scores 12.86 percent. Wire four copies of it together correctly and the number moves.

stories.headline: Agent Skills Work — But Not for the Reason Everyone Assumed
stories.key_takeaway: A controlled study of 8,135 agent trial records finds SKILL.md-style artifacts help by stabilizing execution procedure, not by injecting missing knowledge — and that skill-retrieval precision collapses as libraries grow.

pull_quote.text: skills usually do not work by supplying missing facts. They work by stabilizing action: which setup steps to run, which tool sequence to follow, what intermediate checks to perform, and which recurring pitfalls to avoid.
pull_quote.attribution: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work—Until They Don't

stories.article_excerpt: Every agent framework shipping today assumes the same thing: if you hand a model a written-down procedure, it learns something it did not know.

stories.headline: Three Weeks Into Real Enforcement, the EU AI Office Can Fine Frontier Labs. Its Evaluation Unit Has 36 People.
stories.key_takeaway: The EU AI Office gained real power on 2 August to compel documentation and fine providers up to €15M or 3% of global turnover, but with a 36-person evaluation unit and most member states yet to notify contact points, no formal case has been opened.

pull_quote.text: the resourcing trajectory of the AI Office does not appear aligned with the scale and complexity of its foreseen tasks
pull_quote.attribution: Benifei, Lagodinsky, van Sparrentak, Voss and Vigenin
pull_quote.role: Members of the European Parliament, letter to the Commission

stories.article_excerpt: Three weeks ago, on 2 August, the European Commission's AI Office acquired the legal power to compel the world's largest model providers to hand over documentation.

stories.headline: A Federal Judge Just Refused to Kill a ChatGPT Death Case — and the Product-Liability Theory With It
stories.key_takeaway: A federal refusal to stay Lyons v. OpenAI keeps a wrongful-death case alive alongside twelve coordinated California state suits, and the operative theory across all of them is product liability — not territory Section 230 has historically covered.

pull_quote.text: Even though the cases share certain key facts and issues, there is doubt that resolution of the state court proceedings will resolve this matter, and so a Colorado River stay or dismissal is not warranted.
pull_quote.role: Chief Judge, U.S. District Court, N.D. Cal.

data_points.label: Causes of action pleaded by both estates
Date the motion to dismiss was denied

stories.article_excerpt: On April 13, Chief Judge Richard Seeborg of the Northern District of California refused to get out of the way of a case testing whether a chatbot is a product.
